newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFin hits record high on debt news, U.S..
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFin hits record high on debt news, U.S..

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose to record highs on Friday on news creditor banks had signed up the target sum to reschedule the London Club debt and on the rally in U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.

Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Friday Russia's bank creditors had agreed in principle to reschedule debts of over $20 billion, the critical mass needed for a global rescheduling of $35 billion of debt to go ahead.
Dealers said prices also got a boost from the jump in U.S.Treasuries after tame U.S. consumer price data.
"MinFins started rising at once and the trend could continue," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
But dealers added MinFin bond prices had been rising the whole day as the market was looking up ahead of the announcement of the rating for Russia's Eurobonds.
"Prices have been rising since the very beginning. They bounced back later on profit-taking after a good rise in the recent days," said Avtobank dealer Pavel Afanasyev.
Dealers said the prices of the third, fourth and fifth tranches had met resistance at 77.40, 50.60 and 33.60, respectively.
It was more difficult to determine such levels for the 2006 and 2011 maturities given their lower liquidity inside Russia.
Dealers said a one-month delay in issuing Eurobonds was unlikely to stop the rise.

Kasyanov said Russia hoped to issue its planned Eurobond late next month or early in November. Other Russian officials said previously Russia would issue a first $300-$500 million Eurobond in late September or early October.
"Everybody thinks MinFins are undervalued, and buying is rather active," one dealer said, noting buying from both Russian and foreign operators.
